unit.title: Verbal periphrases
unit.subtitle: acabar de, volver a, dejar de, ponerse a, llevar + gerundio, seguir

grammar.title: Little verb combos that make you sound fluent
grammar.intro: A perífrasis verbal is a small team of verbs — an auxiliary + an infinitive or gerund — that expresses when, how or how long an action happens. They're the shortcuts native speakers reach for constantly: “I've just arrived”, “I've been waiting an hour”, “it started to rain”. Learn the pattern each one takes and your Spanish jumps forward.

sections.heading: acabar de, volver a, dejar de + infinitive
sections.body: These three all take the infinitive. Acabar de = to have just done. Volver a = to do again. Dejar de = to stop doing.

ex.en: I stopped smoking a year ago.

sections.heading: ponerse a and estar a punto de + infinitive
sections.body: Ponerse a + infinitive = to start suddenly. Estar a punto de + infinitive = to be about to, right on the edge of doing it.

ex.es: El tren está a punto de salir.
ex.en: The train is about to leave.

sections.heading: llevar and seguir + gerund (duration)
sections.body: These take the gerundio (-ando/-iendo). Llevar + time + gerund = how long you've been doing something (use this, not hace, for ongoing duration). Seguir + gerund = to keep on doing.
conj: I've been studying for two years

ex.en: I've been studying Spanish for two years.
Even though it's late, I'm still working.

takeaways: Infinitive combos: acabar de (have just), volver a (again), dejar de (stop), ponerse a (start suddenly), estar a punto de (about to).
Acabo de llegar = I've just arrived; volví a llamar = I called again; dejé de fumar = I stopped smoking.
Duration takes the gerundio: llevo una hora esperando — use llevar, not hace, for ongoing duration.
seguir + gerundio = to keep doing: sigo trabajando.

mistakes.why: Llevar for duration takes the gerundio (estudiando), not a conjugated verb.
For ongoing duration with a gerund, use llevar, not hace.
Acabar de takes the infinitive, not the gerundio.

exercises.prompt: No te preocupes, ___ comer. Ya no tengo hambre.
exercises.prompt_en: Don't worry, I've just eaten. I'm not hungry anymore.
I've been waiting for the bus for an hour.
exercises.no: For ongoing duration + gerund, use llevar: “Llevo una hora esperando”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I've been studying Spanish for two years.”
exercises.no: Duration takes llevar + gerundio → “Llevo dos años estudiando español”.

exercises.prompt: De repente se ___ a llover. (ponerse, él/ello)
exercises.hint: ponerse a + infinitive — a sudden start, in the past
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Inicio repentino → se puso a llover.
exercises.no: A sudden start → “se puso a llover”.

exercises.prompt: Match each periphrasis to its meaning.

exercises.tts: El tren está a punto de salir.
accepted: el tren esta a punto de salir
exercises.translation: The train is about to leave.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “El tren está a punto de salir.”
exercises.no: It was: “El tren está a punto de salir.” (The train is about to leave.)

exercises.scenario: A friend calls while you're busy 📞

lines.speaker: Carmen
lines.en: Are you still at the office? It's really late!

options.text: Sí, llevo tres horas trabajando y sigo aquí.
Sí, hace tres horas trabajando y sigo aquí.
Sí, llevo tres horas trabajo y sigo aquí.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! llevar + tiempo + gerundio, natural y correcto.
exercises.no: Duration = llevar + gerundio → “llevo tres horas trabajando”.

exercises.say: Acabo de llegar y llevo diez minutos esperando
exercises.en: I've just arrived and I've been waiting ten minutes
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.

vocab.en: to have been doing (for X time)
